text:
Ville Koivunen came to Pittsburgh as one of the prospects in the Jake Guentzel trade, and in his second NHL season he is holding his own. Seven points in 18 games at about 14 minutes a night matches his entire total from 39 games last season, and he is a little ahead of where forwards drafted in his range usually start (0.39 points a game against a median of 0.30).

He isn't a shooter. Fourteen shots in 18 games, no hits at all, and a game built on moving the puck: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him exiting with possession 63% of the time last season, in a small sample. Evolving-Hockey, also on limited minutes, had opponents getting fewer chances with him on the ice.

There is a little luck in the results. Pittsburgh has scored 2.7 more goals than its chances deserved with him on, and his own finishing is right on his expected goals. His last ten games produced three points, in line with his chances. Our range sees about 28 points by season's end. For a 23-year-old on a losing team, regular minutes and staying even in them is a decent start.
